question.text:
At a constant temperature, which of the following aqueous solutions will have the maximum vapour pressure?
(Mol. wt. NaCl = 58.5,  H 2 SO 4  = 98 .0 g mol −1 )

solution.text: One molar <math> <mrow>  <mtext>(1</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>M)</mtext></mrow></math> aqueous solution is more concentrated than one molal aqueous solution of the same solute. In solution, <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></math> provides three ions. While <math > <mrow>  <mtext>NaCl</mtext></mrow></math> provides two ions. Hence, vapour pressure of solution of <math > <mrow>  <mtext>NaCl</mtext></mrow></math> is higher (as it gives less ions). Therefore, <math > <mrow>  <mtext>1</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>molal</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>NaCl</mtext></mrow></math> will have the maximum vapour pressure.
